Daniel Okafor-Reyes
Backend Software Engineer

Lisbon, Portugal | daniel.okafor-reyes@example.com | +351 555 010 202 | linkedin.com/in/daniel-okafor-reyes-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Backend Software Engineer with 7 years of professional experience building and operating Java backend services for insurance and travel products. Experienced in REST API design, relational databases, Kafka event-driven integrations, automated testing, and cloud deployment on AWS EKS. Improved production API performance and reliability, and participates in a regular on-call rota. Fluent in English and Portuguese; conversational in Spanish.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Backend: Java (8–17), Spring Boot, Spring MVC, Spring Data JPA, Hibernate, Kotlin (basic)
APIs and messaging: REST, OpenAPI, Kafka, RabbitMQ
Databases and performance: PostgreSQL, Oracle, Redis, JPA query optimization
Cloud and delivery: AWS (EKS, S3, SQS), Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, Jenkins, CI/CD
Testing and tools: JUnit 5, Testcontainers, Git, Linux

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Backend Engineer | Tejo Insurance Tech | Lisbon
Jan 2022–Present
- Develop and maintain 7 Java 17 / Spring Boot microservices for policy quoting and claims intake.
- Designed and versioned the REST API for partner quoting integration, used by 12 broker partners and documented with OpenAPI.
- Produce and consume Kafka events for the claims workflow; introduced idempotent consumers and an outbox table, eliminating duplicate claim records.
- Reduced quote endpoint p99 latency from 1.8 seconds to 450 milliseconds by adding Redis caching and resolving N+1 queries in JPA.
- Deploy services to Kubernetes on AWS EKS using Helm charts and Jenkins pipelines; participate in an on-call rota one week per month.

Software Developer | Viajar Online S.A. | Porto
Sep 2019–Dec 2021
- Built booking and payment features in a Java 11 / Spring MVC monolith backed by Oracle.
- Wrote integration tests with Testcontainers, increasing payments-module test coverage from 35% to 70%.
- Contributed to splitting the monolith by extracting the notifications service using Spring Boot and RabbitMQ.

Junior Developer (Internship, then Full-Time) | CodeFarol Lda | Porto
Jul 2018–Aug 2019
- Maintained PHP and later Java applications for small business clients.

EDUCATION
BSc Informatics Engineering | Atlantic Polytechnic Institute | 2018

LANGUAGES
English (fluent) | Portuguese (fluent) | Spanish (conversational)

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is clear, well structured, concise, and professionally written. It presents seven years of relevant backend experience with strong quantified evidence: 12 broker partners, a reduction in p99 latency from 1.8 seconds to 450 milliseconds, and test coverage improvement from 35% to 70%. The experience bullets demonstrate ownership of APIs, event-driven integrations, performance, cloud deployment, and on-call responsibilities. The main content limitation is not a writing defect: the candidate's source information does not establish Python, schema-migration, observability, logistics, or Dutch/French experience.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document uses standard section headings, conventional reverse-chronological employment history, readable bullets, and ATS-friendly text formatting. It contains strong matching keywords including Java, Spring Boot, REST, OpenAPI, Kafka, PostgreSQL, Docker, AWS, EKS, Kubernetes, automated testing, Jenkins, CI/CD, JUnit, and Testcontainers. Its likely ATS screening probability is high for a comparable-language backend profile, but lower for filters requiring explicit Python or FastAPI. The CV should not add Python, FastAPI, Terraform, GitHub Actions, or observability tools because they are not supported by the original candidate information. A small keyword improvement would be to make API versioning and integration testing more explicit in the skills section.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns strongly with the role's comparable-language backend requirement: it shows seven years of professional Java backend-services experience, REST API design, Kafka, Docker, AWS EKS, Kubernetes, PostgreSQL, query-performance work, automated integration testing, CI/CD, and fluent English. It also supports the team's reliability and ownership expectations through quantified production improvements and a regular on-call rota. The candidate's source information does not show professional Python experience or stated willingness to work mainly in Python; this is a role-fit gap rather than a CV defect. It also does not show schema migrations, Terraform, Prometheus/Grafana/OpenTelemetry, logistics or supply-chain experience, EDI formats, or Dutch/French. The document does show technical decision-making through its descriptions of idempotent consumers, an outbox table, Redis caching, and N+1 query resolution, although it does not explicitly use the phrase 'technical trade-offs'.
critique.improvement_instructions: MINOR ENHANCEMENT — In the TECHNICAL SKILLS section, change the APIs and messaging line from "REST, OpenAPI, Kafka, RabbitMQ" to "REST APIs, OpenAPI, API versioning, Kafka, RabbitMQ". API versioning is directly supported by the Tejo Insurance Tech experience and more closely matches the job description's terminology. Also change "Testcontainers" in the Testing and tools line to "Automated integration testing, JUnit 5, Testcontainers"; this makes the supported testing capability more immediately visible to ATS screening without overstating the candidate's experience.
